newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Mixed signals about health of Vietnam's President.
newsitem.headline: Mixed signals about health of Vietnam's President.

text.p: Vietnam's President Anh was being treated in a Hanoi hospital on Sunday for blood pressure problems, but there were mixed reports about the severity of his condition.
Medical staff at Hanoi's prestigious 108 Army hospital said the 75-year-old president was being treated there but declined to discuss details of the case.
One government official, who declined to be named, said Anh, 75, was unconscious and suffering haemorrhaging around the brain. He said doctors were having difficulties dealing with his condition.
But others played down the reports. A hospital staff member said Anh had been ill during the past week but was recovering and might be discharged later on Sunday.
Hanoi's political rumour mill had been awash with speculation about the president's health over the past week because of a longer than usual absence from public view.
An informed political source said on Sunday he had undergone a routine health check-up earlier in the week but was then readmitted to hospital on Friday.
Newspapers reported he had signed a decision formalising changes to Vietnam's cabinet as recently as November 12.
General Anh is one of three top leaders in Vietnam and was appointed president in September 1992.
He is seen by Western observers as representing the conservative and military elements of Vietnam's communist government and is ranked number two in the elite politburo.
The next most senior politburo member from a military background is 64-year-old Lieutenant-General Le Kha Phieu.

The other members of the leadership triumvirate are Party chief Do Muoi, 79, seen as occupying a central and stabilising role, and Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, 73, considered a firm supporter of economic reforms.
